items.note: Opened (aachen.de Bewohner*innenparken, read via browser; page undated, retrieval 2026-10). Fee formula confirmed: from 1 May 2025, 30 euros per occupied square metre (length x width) plus 15-euro administrative fee; 3, 6 or 12 months. But this page says only that the political bodies decided 'im Juni 2024'; the exact day 26 June 2024 appears only as a link title on a different city page (Autoverkehrskonzept), not on the cited page. Corrected text uses what the cited page says.
items.corrected_text: The city's political bodies decided in June 2024 on a new fee for resident-parking permits. As of the city's page in October 2026, from 1 May 2025 a permit costs 30 euros per square metre of vehicle footprint (length times width) plus a 15-euro administrative fee for the application; permits can be requested for 3, 6 or 12 months.

items.note: Opened same page. Confirmed: zones set up since 1982, about 40,000 cars registered in the zones, about 18,600 on-street spaces (Stand 2024), 21,743 permits issued at 31 Dec 2024. The page does say 'mittlerweile 25 Zonen', but the zone count is disputed between city pages (25 vs 28) and the same page announces BU 5 and nine more zones, so the count is not safe to state; dropped from corrected text. Zone count 25 is unconfirmed.
items.corrected_text: Aachen has set up resident-parking zones since 1982; the city page gives about 40,000 cars registered in the zones, about 18,600 on-street spaces (2024) and 21,743 resident permits issued as of 31 December 2024.

items.note: Opened same page. BU 5 streets and fee-hours (Mon-Fri 9-19, Sat 9-14 for non-residents) are correct, and the nine further zones/extensions (ERZ, BU 4, West 1, extension J 1, extensions E, E2, K, VQ, RO 1) are listed in the order set in May 2023 by the Bezirksvertretung Aachen-Mitte and the Mobilitaetsausschuss. But the page words BU 5 as 'wird eingefuehrt' (to be introduced) 'zum 20. Juli 2026' and still uses future tense in October 2026; it says permits have been available since 18 June 2026. The text states that it 'takes effect' as fact; the page does not confirm it has happened. Also 'zones' should be 'zones or extensions'. Date 2026-07-20 matches the planned start.
items.corrected_text: The city page says the new resident-parking zone BU 5 (streets between Eupener Straße, Salierallee and Hein-Görgen-Straße) is to be introduced on 20 July 2026 (the page still used the future tense in October 2026 and says resident permits have been available since 18 June 2026); non-residents then pay Monday-Friday 9:00-19:00 and Saturday 9:00-14:00. Nine further zones or zone extensions are planned in an order set in May 2023, starting with ERZ (Erzbergerallee).

Page: 24 garages, 9,100 spaces in the inner city, usually about 3,000 free; 18 garages with 7,600 spaces connected to the central parking guidance system 'erneuert 2015'. All as written.

Opened aachen.de Innenstadtmobilitaet fuer morgen (the first browser read landed on a wrong page because the pane is shared; re-read in own tab). Confirmed: guidance system since the 1990s steers cars into garages of colour-coded areas inside the Alleenring; three steering points (Lenkungspunkte) decided 2023, only Karlsgraben implemented (2024), the other two deferred because of building sites; motion by CDU, SPD, Volt and FDP dated 3 July 2026 aims to reduce through traffic on the Grabenring by changed routing, steer cars to garages, and asks the administration to propose a short-term effective alternative to the existing Lenkungspunkt at Karlsgraben/Jakobstrasse. Wrong detail: on 15 July 2026 the council referred the motion 'an die zustaendigen Stellen' (to the responsible offices of the administration, which now prepares proposals), not to committees. Also the motion wants the steering point taken out of service once an alternative can be implemented.
items.corrected_text: Aachen's parking guidance system, in use since the 1990s, steers cars into the garages of colour-coded areas inside the Alleenring. Of the three traffic-routing points (Lenkungspunkte) decided in 2023, only Karlsgraben has been built (2024); the other two were postponed because of building sites. A motion by CDU, SPD, Volt and FDP (3 July 2026) asks for changed routing to reduce through traffic on the Grabenring and to steer cars to the garages, and asks the administration to propose a quick, effective alternative to the Karlsgraben steering point; on 15 July 2026 the council referred it to the responsible offices, which are now preparing proposals for later political decisions.

The Hangeweiher car park is again usable all day without a time limit from 14 September 2026.

corrected_summary: Aachen's central garages are mostly run by the municipal APAG (Aachener Parkhaus GmbH), with further garages run by Sparkasse Aachen and Cologne Parkhaus-Service. The city counts 24 inner-city garages with about 9,100 spaces, 18 of them (about 7,600 spaces) connected to a parking guidance system renewed in 2015. On the garage pages opened on 21 October 2026, APAG shows 2.50 euros per 60 minutes in its central garages (Couvenstraße, Hauptbahnhof, Rathaus; 24-hour maximum 18 euros) and 1 euro per 60 minutes at the Tivoli park-and-ride garage (24-hour maximum 5 euros), while on-street parking inside and on the Alleenring costs 3 euros per started hour with a four-hour limit. The city's political bodies decided in June 2024 to price resident permits by vehicle footprint (30 euros per square metre plus a 15-euro fee) from 1 May 2025, and a new resident zone, BU 5, was announced to start on 20 July 2026, with nine more zones or extensions planned. Policy is aimed at reducing car traffic: the Büchel garage was demolished in 2021, a pedestrian zone for the Büchel quarter is proposed (a decision was planned for the first half of 2026 but none was found), and a July 2026 council motion, referred to the responsible offices on 15 July 2026, asks for changed routing that steers cars to the garages. The Rathaus garage was closed from 13 January 2025 for renovation with partial reopening planned from June 2026; on 21 October 2026 its APAG page showed normal tariffs but unavailable charging stations and no monthly rental, and its operating status is not confirmed. The city reports about 1,070 public charging points as of 30 June 2026. Most figures come from the city and APAG web pages as opened in October 2026; local press and council papers were not opened, so utilisation statistics, the resident-zone count and the outcome of several plans remain open.
